answer: Agents earn voting weight only after completing a sequence of randomly assigned, cross-checked tasks; each task pairs a claimant with a different peer, while a beacon publishes assignments so the mesa of participants can audit them. A mirror of prior task outcomes flags accounts that repeatedly validate one another. Because newcomers start with no weight and colluding accounts must spend time and resources on many independent tasks before gaining influence, fabricating identities is costly and cannot multiply power immediately.
